This toolkit helps faculty, committees, chairs, deans, and other stakeholders create, review, and advance curriculum proposals through the University’s approval process. It outlines roles, expectations, processes, and resources to support accurate, efficient proposals and effective shared governance.
The Playbook focuses on process, not content. Faculty remain the subject-matter experts on academic purpose, curriculum, and learning outcomes; this resource provides the framework for moving proposals smoothly through review and approval.
It is designed so that everyone can start where they need help without having to sort through guidance intended for other roles.

Specialization Description
Tags: specializations
Short Description: The University Catalog description of a program specialization, including its specialization-specific curriculum and any additional requirements for completion.
Specialization Description
The University Catalog description of the requirements for completing a specialization within an academic program, including the specialization-specific courses and credits required in addition to the program’s core requirements, as well as any additional specialization-specific requirements.

Descriptive overview: A brief paragraph explaining the purpose and significance of the specialization.
Course Requirements
Important: Do not include program requirements in the specialization description.
Only include the requirements of the specialization in the specialization description, and exclude the core requirements to the program. The specialization
A specialization is an addition to the academic program, not a second listing of the program’s requirements. Students complete the requirements of the program and, where applicable, the additional requirements of their chosen specialization. The specialization description should therefore include only the requirements that are specific to that specialization.
Repeating the program requirements within the specialization could imply that students must complete those requirements again as part of the specialization. Keeping program-wide requirements in the program description and specialization-specific requirements in the specialization description makes it clear which requirements apply to the program as a whole and which are additional requirements for the specialization.
(For ABMs only) Courses that are able to be double-counted

A minimum GPA average of 2.00 must be earned in the specialization courses (UM 8.20.61)
Half of the credits required for the specialization must be earned at URI (UM 8.20.61)
A maximum of one third of the total credits required for a master’s program may be double counted for an ABM program. (UM 8.30.19)

New Temporary & Permanent Course Email
Date: May 31, 2027 (2027-05-31)
Tags: Temp Course Email
New Temporary & Permanent Course Email
The New Temporary & Permanent Course Email is distributed to all faculty, deans, and associate and assistant deans on the last weekday of each month. Recipients then have seven days to submit comments to the CASC Chair, GEC Chair, or Dean of the Graduate School regarding any potential or perceived content overlap involving a new temporary or permanent course.
The email serves two purposes:
Provides notice of upcoming Faculty Senate review. Courses included in the email have already been reviewed and approved by their respective College Curriculum Committees and will next be reviewed by the appropriate Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee: CASC, GEC, or Graduate Council.
Provides an opportunity to identify potential content overlap. College Curriculum Committees may review the courses included in the email to identify any potential or perceived overlap with courses offered or proposed by other colleges. Any concerns can then be raised before the courses proceed to Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee review.

All new courses must be certified as having been reviewed by the faculty of the originating academic organization. Certification must be provided by the appropriate authority, which may include the Department Chair, Area Coordinator, or, in some cases, the College Curriculum Committee Chair.
The proposer should leave this section blank. The Department Chair or other authorized curriculum reviewer will complete the certification by checking the box to confirm that the course has been reviewed by the appropriate faculty, entering their name, and providing the date of certification.
Once the proposal reaches the course certification step in the workflow, it cannot move forward until the designated certifier completes this section.

Content Overlap
Tags: courses,programs,specializations
Short Description: Proposers should review existing curricula and ensure that proposed courses, programs, and specializations do not contain substantial content overlap.
Content Overlap
Proposed courses, programs, and specializations are reviewed for potential content overlap with existing curricula. Proposers should review existing curricula and ensure that proposed courses, programs, and specializations do not contain substantial actual or perceived content overlap.
Early consultation with potentially affected academic units may help identify concerns, clarify distinctions between offerings, and support an efficient review process.
A letter of support, which may be provided as an email from an affected department chair, can be uploaded to the Kuali proposal to document (a) that both departments have considered potential content overlap; (b) communication between the affected department and the department proposing the curriculum; and (c) the affected department’s support for the proposed curriculum.

Program Description
The University Catalog description of the requirements for completing an academic program, including the courses and credits required for the major, General Education, and free electives, as well as any additional program-specific requirements.

Descriptive overview: A brief paragraph explaining the purpose of the program and the significance of the degree or major.
Specializations: The specializations (sub-plans) should be listed by name, but the requirements should not be listed in the program description.
Major Requirements: Listed, required courses
Professional Electives: Students choose from a list of courses selected specifically to align with the content of the program
Free Electives: Students are free to choose. Must provide a credit amount, minimum 6 credits for undergraduate degrees are required
Cumulative GPA and/or major GPA requirements

An undergraduate student’s field of study is called the “major” (UM 8.20.40)
A graduate student’s field of study is called the “program” (UM 8.20.40)
Undergraduate programs are required to have a minimum or 120 credits, and a maximum of 148 (UM 8.21.10)
Undergraduate programs shall include at least 6 credits of free electives (UM 8.21.10)
General Education requirements shall apply to all undergraduate programs (UM 8.21.11)
A cumulative average of at least 2.00 is required to graduate from all undergraduate degrees. (UM 8.22.10)
Master’s degree programs with thesis require a minimum of 30 credits. 18 must be from content-based courses, 6 must be thesis courses. (GSM 7.44.1)
Master’s degree programs without thesis require a minimum of 30 credits. (GSM 7.45.1)
Doctoral students must complete a Program of Study with a minimum of 64 credit hours beyond the undergraduate degree (GSM 7.54) (See GSM sections 7.54 and 7.21)

18 or more credits of related studies offered by one or more departments or programs and sponsored by a faculty member. (UM 8.20.50)
At least 12 credits at the 200-level or above ( UM 8.20.51)
At least 8 credits must be earned at URI (UM 8.20.51)
Minimum GPA average of 2.0 must be earned in the minor’s required courses (UM 8.20.51)
A maximum of two courses can apply to both the major and minor field of study (UM 8.20.52)

Undergraduate certificates generally require 15-21 credits of coursework (UM 8.20.70)
Undergraduate certificates are available to degree seeking and certificate-only seeking undergraduate students (UM 8.20.70)
Undergraduate certificate courses may not be pass/fail (UM 8.20.71)
Graduate certificates require 12 credits minimum, 16 credits maximum. (GSM Appendix J.1.1)
Post-master’s graduate certificates require 12 credits minimum, 18 credits maximum. (GSM Appendix J.1.1)
